$comment: Generated from Rust deserialization types by game schema. Do not edit. Runtime semantic validators additionally check ranges, references, formats and capabilities.

AudioCategory.description:
How a game groups its sounds, and what the engine does about the grouping.

The engine does not name `bgm` or `sfx`: the taxonomy is the game's. It owns
only the rules, because they decide which source survives a switch, and that
is world state a test asserts.

The reserved fields exist so the declaration shape does not have to change
when they are implemented. Declaring one is an **error**, never a silent
no-op: a game believing it configured something it did not is the hardest
kind of audio bug to find.

exclusive.description:
Only one loop in this category plays at a time; starting another begins
stopping the previous one.

volume.description:
The bus level this category starts at, the way a mixer group has a
volume before anything plays. A settings screen changes it at runtime.

UiPreviewSpec.description: One reachable screen the layout gate should inspect.

input_sequence.description: Project-relative per-frame input replay that reaches this screen.

overlap_policy.description: Project-relative exact image-behind-control overlap policy for this preview.

VerifyConfig.description:
The gates this project wants `verify` to run.

The default order is the engine's opinion, not a law. A project that draws
no screen, or that is mid-way through acquiring assets, should be able to
say so once in its config rather than teaching its author to read past a
red line — a gate people learn to ignore is worse than a gate that says it
is advisory.

command.description:
Reserved: a project-owned command as a gate. Declaring it is an error in
this build rather than a step that silently never runs.

required.description: A failing advisory gate is reported and does not fail the run.

VerifyStepSpec.description: One declared gate: either the bare id, or the id with its settings.

audio.description:
Sound categories and the rules between them.

Undeclared means no rules, not no sound: a game can still play and loop
without ever naming a category. Categories exist to say what happens
*between* sounds, which is the part the engine owns.

job_scripts.description: Isolated Luau job modules, keyed by operation name.

systems.description:
Engine systems this game explicitly turns on or off.

Anything not declared keeps the engine default; the engine rejects
unknown ids instead of treating a typo as a disabled system.

ui_previews.description:
Screens `verify` must check the layout of.

Without this only the opening screen is ever drawn, so a broken win or
lose screen passes every gate. Each entry says how to reach a screen,
the same way `test_files` says how to reach a state worth asserting.

verify.description:
Which gates `verify` runs, in what order, and which of them are
advisory.

Undeclared means the engine's default order with every gate required.
